text:
Maya Singh: Incoming from ProspectOps (Acme)  they pushed back on our SIG BCP/DR answers and specifically asked for: 1) concrete RTO/RPO examples for Hosted vs Dedicated, 2) proof of backups and retention, and 3) a short list of shareable artifacts. Need a concise packet we can attach to the RFP by EOD. Who can own?

Theo Park: I can take the writeup. Prefer to give ranges + explicit caveats so we don't overpromise. Will include a one-line example scenario for Hosted failover.

Riley Chen: From infra: Hosted example: automated cross-region routing kicks in after health checks/route updates propagate (~5-10s), but capacity warm-up and session rehydration drive RTO. We can say typical RTO <15 minutes for stateless requests; note stateful sessions depend on customer config.

Nina Patel: Security side: backups are encrypted at rest + in transit. Control plane metadata: async cross-region replication + daily snapshots. Default retention 30 days; enterprise customers can enable 90/365 or export. We can provide redacted DR test summaries and our quarterly DR playbook excerpt under NDA.

Theo Park: Draft SIG-friendly block (pasteable):

```
- RTO: Hosted: target <15 minutes for automated cross-region reroute for stateless APIs under our smart-routing policies; Dedicated: typically 1-4 hours for single-region hardware incidents unless multi-region reserved capacity is configured per contract.
- RPO: Hosted: in-memory caches are best-effort (seconds-to-minutes); persistent control-plane/customer artifacts use cross-region async replication and daily snapshots (default RPO up to 1 hour); Dedicated/Private: configurable replication/snapshot cadence for tighter RPOs.
- Backups & Retention: Encrypted daily snapshots retained 30 days by default. Optional extended retention and on-demand export available for enterprise customers.
- Failover: Automated routing, model-variant fallbacks, canary deploys, and automatic rollback. Customers requiring deterministic failover can purchase reserved multi-region capacity on Dedicated.
- SLA: Hosted API: paid tiers target 99.9% monthly uptime. Dedicated: enterprise SLA tiers up to 99.95%/99.99% based on contract and reserved capacity.
- Evidence: We can share DR runbook excerpts, recent DR test summaries (redacted), SOC2 summary, and architecture diagrams under NDA.
```

Theo Park: Add short scenario example below the block so reviewer has concrete numbers: 

```
Scenario (Hosted): Primary region experiences partial outage at t=0. Automated health checks + smart-routing mark affected nodes; routing change propagates ~30-90s; new requests served from healthy region. Application-level session rehydration (if configured with persistent replication) can be complete within 5-15 minutes; best-effort for in-memory state.
```

Nina Patel: Suggest small wording tweaks: change "up to 1 hour" -> "default RPO up to 1 hour for persistent artifacts; accelerated replication available via config". Also note quarterly DR exercises and a public changelog of major DR learnings (redacted).

Riley Chen: I'll add a line about snapshots being encrypted with KMS and tested restores during DR exercises. We run restores at least quarterly from snapshots to verify retention.

Maya Singh: Good. Also attach a checklist to send with packet: runbook excerpt, last 2 DR test summaries, SOC2 summary, infra topology diagram, SLA schedule, and contacts for escalation. Keep filenames simple for legal: "runbook_excerpt_redacted.pdf", "dr_tests_q1q2.pdf", "soc2_summary_2025.pdf".

legal-bot: Reminder: Do not attach raw SOC2 report to external parties; provide SOC2 summary and offer full report under executed NDA only. Ensure all shared artifacts have PII redacted.

Theo Park: I'll finalize the SIG block with Nina/Riley edits and produce a single-page PDF summary + list of artifacts. Target to drop into the RFP portal by 17:30 PST.

ops-bot: Action item created: RFP - Acme evidence packet. Attachments required: runbook excerpt, DR test summaries, SOC2 summary, infra diagram, SLA schedule. Tag owner=Theo Park, due=17:30 PST.

Maya Singh: Thanks. Once uploaded I'll confirm and send to ProspectOps. :thumbsup:
